records.context: one row per cell with any read: ``keys``, ``reads``, ``matched`` (exact or corrected), ``exact``, ``corrected``, ``ambiguous``, ``collision``, ``out_of_library``, ``barcodes`` (distinct callable barcodes), ``prefix``, ``guide``, ``gene`` and ``level`` of the top barcode (empty unless ``perfect`` or ``great``), ``top_reads``, ``top_exact``, ``top_share`` (of matched reads), ``second_reads``, ``has_exact_read`` and ``quality``. Under ``'weighted_majority'`` (:data:`WEIGHTED_CLASSES`) the top barcode is the one with the most weight, and five columns are added. ``weight_top`` and ``weight_total`` are the summed read weights of the top barcode and of the cell. ``d_weight_top`` is the summed distance term of the top barcode's reads, and ``g_median_top`` their median nucleus distance (NaN without one). ``bleed_discounted`` counts the barcodes the neighbour discount weighed down.

Under ``'weighted_majority'`` (:data:`WEIGHTED_CLASSES`) the top barcode is the one with the most weight, and five columns are added. ``weight_top`` and ``weight_total`` are the summed read weights of the top barcode and of the cell. ``d_weight_top`` is the summed distance term of the top barcode's reads, and ``g_median_top`` their median nucleus distance (NaN without one). ``bleed_discounted`` counts the barcodes the neighbour discount weighed down.

records.context: ``ops_read_distance_weight`` (item 988, alpha). ``'off'`` keeps the weights above. ``'decay'`` multiplies each read's weight by its distance term, and ``'distance_only'`` uses the distance term alone. The distance term is 1 up to ``interior_px`` and ``exp(-(g - interior_px) / decay_px)`` beyond it, at least ``min_weight``. The distance term is 1 up to ``interior_px`` and ``exp(-(g - interior_px) / decay_px)`` beyond it, at least ``min_weight``. A one-read guide then needs its quality times its distance term to reach ``single_read_quality``.
records.translation: ``ops_read_distance_weight`` (item 988, alfa). ``'off'`` mantém os pesos acima. ``'decay'`` multiplica o peso de cada leitura pelo seu termo de distância, e ``'distance_only'`` usa apenas o termo de distância. O termo de distância é 1 até ``interior_px`` e ``exp(-(g - interior_px) / decay_px)`` além disso, com no mínimo ``min_weight``. Uma guia com uma única leitura precisa então que a sua qualidade multiplicada pelo seu termo de distância alcance ``single_read_quality``.
